newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND FREES FUEL PRICES ON THURSDAY - FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: POLAND FREES FUEL PRICES ON THURSDAY - FINMIN.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry freed on Thursday prices of domestically produced fuels, it said in a statement.
Polish domestic fuel prices were so far controlled by the ministry while imported fuel was free of any price limits.
"The finance ministry informs that as of February 13 prices of domestically produced engine fuels are freed," it said.

It also said the ministry lifted all administrative limits on profit margins applied to engine fuel trade in leaded and unleaded petrol as well as diesel fuel. The profit margin was so far set at a maximum of 213 zlotys per tonne of fuel.
The ministry also ended a requirement that producers and distributors of fuel had to inform tax offices in advance of price rises, which could then be held up for three months.

The ministry said the administrative control of fuel prices had to be removed because of the sharp rise of engine fuel prices on world markets had led to a wide gap between the cost of cheap domestic fuel and expensive imports.
"It is hard to call this a normal situation," it said.
As a result of the administrative controls Polish refineries suffered losses because they could not offset the rising world crude prices by increasing domestic market prices.
"...this has been hindering the implementation of already begun investment programmes in these companies," the statement said.

The ministry said that the freeing of fuel prices has been forseen in a government programme of restructuring of the oil sector, approved last year, which aims to make the industry competitive before foreign rivals are admitted to the market.
"Without the freeing of prices the realisation of this goal would be impossible," the statement said.

"The freeing of prices will enable free competition between producers and importers and between private and state-owned firms operating on the fuels market. In this way it will support the normal functioning of the Polish economy," the statement said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
